title: When the anesthesiologist goes to the dentist
html: On October 16, 1846, inside the amphitheater of Massachusetts General Hospital, a dentist named William Thomas Green Morton forever changed the fabric of human suffering.1 By administering sulfuric ether to Gilbert Abbott, Morton did more than just facilitate the painless removal of a vascular tumor, he effectively laid the cornerstone for the modern medical specialty of anesthesiology and catapulted all surgery to new heights. It is a historical debt that anesthesiologists acknowledge with profound gratitude.
